children: Shares across the Tata group rose sharply on Thursday after the Tata Sons board voted by majority to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as Executive Chairman for a fresh five-year term, a move the majority shareholder, Tata Trusts, immediately contested as a legal nullity.

Tata Investment Corporation led the rally, rising 5.47 per cent on the BSE. Tata Chemicals gained 6.6 per cent, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles climbed 4.52 per cent, Tata Motors rose 2.82 per cent, and Tata Steel was up 2.82 per cent. The broader Nifty Tata 25 Cap index closed 1 per cent higher at 14,015.75. IT major TCS, which had risen as much as 3 per cent intraday, pared gains to end 0.21 per cent higher. Titan Company was the outlier, falling 1.14 per cent.
Read also: Tata Sons board-room battle: Stalemate allowed chairman to vote on his own reappointment

The board decision came after Chandrasekaran, whose current term ends on February 20, 2027, wrote to the board on August 12, 2026, saying he would not offer himself for reappointment. On September 3, 2026, the Nomination Remuneration Committee unanimously resolved to request him to reconsider. At Thursday’s board meeting, Chandrasekaran acceded to that request, and the board resolved by majority vote to reappoint him.

The reappointment, however, has run into a direct legal challenge. Tata Trusts, which holds approximately 66 per cent of Tata Sons’ equity, said the resolution is “a legal nullity.” In a press release, the Trusts stated that under the Articles of Association, appointing a Chairman requires a majority of the Trusts’ nominee directors to vote in favour, and since Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts and one of the two nominee directors, voted against the resolution, it cannot stand.

“In so far as the Tata Trusts are concerned, the intimation made by the Chairman vide his communication dated 12 August 2026 has been duly accepted and has attained finality,” Noel Tata said in a statement recorded at the board meeting.it is now time to move on.”

The Trusts said they had formally accepted Chandrasekaran’s August decision and had already asked the company to form a selection committee for a successor under its Articles. Noel Tata also submitted a legal opinion obtained from Justice Dr DY Chandrachud, former Chief Justice of India, supporting the Trusts’ position, though the board did not take note of it.
RBI decision adds to Tata Sons uncertainty

The backdrop to this dispute includes a separate regulatory issue: the Reserve Bank of India has rejected Tata Sons’ application to de-register as a non-banking finance company, which triggers a public listing requirement, a move that itself has divided the board.

“It is taking twists and turns. The board has now taken a conscious decision on the five-year extension, after Chandra’s tenure had been in limbo for some time. But the twist is that it is clearly opposed by Noel Tata. The entire episode is unfolding as a long saga, and we need to wait and see what actually happens,” said Kranthi Baithini, director of equity strategy at WealthMills Securities.

Market participants focused on stocks with cross-holdings in Tata Sons, viewing the potential listing as a value-unlocking catalyst. “Sentiment was boosted after the RBI rejected Tata Sons’ proposal to exit the regulatory framework governing Core Investment Companies, reinforcing market expectations that the holding company may eventually pursue a public listing,” said Sunny Agrawal, head of fundamental research at SBI Securities.

The Tata Sons board said it would initiate steps to comply with applicable RBI guidelines and seek guidance from the regulator, Tata Trusts, and other stakeholders on compliance requirements. The legal dispute over the chairmanship is expected to escalate, with the Trusts maintaining that the selection committee process will proceed as directed.

Meanwhile, stocks linked to the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, which has a significant stake in Tata Sons, also saw some positive movement on Thursday. Afcons Infrastructure closed at ₹267.30, up 3.44 per cent on the NSE, though it remains down 41.43 per cent over the past year and 32.33 per cent year-to-date.

Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy ended marginally higher at ₹179.22, up 0.72 per cent, but is off 33.25 per cent over the past year. Among the smaller SP Group-linked counters, Gokak Textiles closed at ₹65.71 on the BSE, up 9.24 per cent for the session, while Forbes and Company ended slightly lower at ₹358.10, down 0.35 per cent.

title: Tata group stocks rise after Chandrasekaran reappointment
